mechanism: fused tiled attention: the s x s scores never round-trip HBM (recomputed in backward)
source: Rabe & Staats (2021), Self-attention Does Not Need O(n^2) Memory, arXiv:2112.05682; Lefaudeux et al. (2022), xFormers
published_value: 59x inference, 32x differentiation; runtime within a few percent of standard attention
note: PyTorch docs link the memory-efficient backend to xFormers; no source states the kernel is derived from it. xFormers README: up to 10x faster (A100, FP16).

mechanism: kernel feature map phi(x)=elu(x)+1 replaces softmax: O(s) prefix state instead of s x s scores
source: Katharopoulos, Vyas, Pappas, Fleuret (2020), Transformers are RNNs, ICML 2020, PMLR 119:5156-5165
note: Katharopoulos et al. (2020) is a listed seminal exception, cited for the linear-attention technique only; its speed figures are not used as evidence (Table 1 exception rule, decided 2026-10-17).

mechanism: fewer K/V heads (heads/4): smaller K/V projections, K/V repeated to all heads
source: Ainslie et al. (2023), GQA, EMNLP 2023; Shazeer (2019), Fast Transformer Decoding, arXiv:1911.02150
published_metric: inference time per sample, T5-XXL, TPUv4 (Table 1)
published_value: GQA-8 0.28 s vs MHA 1.51 s; avg 47.1 vs 47.2
note: Inference speed on an uptrained checkpoint (T5-XXL converted from multi-head with 5% of original pre-training compute), not a pretraining result. heads/4 is not a configuration either paper reports. Shazeer (2019) is cited for the multi-query technique only (seminal exception, method).

mechanism: low-rank factorization of embedding and unembedding through E = 128
source: Lan, Chen, Goodman, Gimpel, Sharma, Soricut (2020), ALBERT, ICLR 2020
note: ALBERT factorizes the input embedding only; the output-side mirror is the thesis's extension.

mechanism: drops mean-centering and bias: fewer reductions and elementwise ops per norm
source: Zhang & Sennrich (2019), Root Mean Square Layer Normalization, NeurIPS 2019
note: Zhang & Sennrich (2019) is cited for the RMSNorm technique only, to be added to Chapter II's seminal-exception list; its running-time figures are not used as evidence (decided 2026-10-17). Efficiency evidence: Liger (rmsnorm_fused) and this study.

mechanism: same RMSNorm function through F.rms_norm (fused CUDA kernel where available): isolates algorithm from implementation
source: Zhang & Sennrich (2019), NeurIPS 2019 (algorithm); Hsu et al. (2024), Liger Kernel: Efficient Triton Kernels for LLM Training, arXiv:2410.10989 (fused kernel benchmark)
published_metric: execution time and peak memory, fused Triton RMSNorm vs eager HF-style RMSNorm, A100 80GB, hidden 16384 (Sec 4.1, Fig 2d/3d)
published_value: about 7x faster; about 3x less peak memory
note: Fused vs eager RMSNorm, not RMSNorm vs LayerNorm. Baseline identified from the repo benchmark script (benchmark_rms_norm.py, custom LlamaRMSNorm in eager ops); the paper says only 'baseline implementations'. Precision and sequence length not stated. Venue: arXiv preprint; repo BibTeX lists the CODEML workshop at ICML 2025 (archival status unconfirmed) and adds an 11th author (Zhipeng Wang). No published fused-RMSNorm vs fused-LayerNorm benchmark found.

mechanism: same rotary function compiled by torch.compile (Inductor) into fused kernels: one read and one write of Q and K instead of six eager operators
source: Hsu et al. (2024), Liger Kernel: Efficient Triton Kernels for LLM Training, arXiv:2410.10989 (fused RoPE kernel)
published_metric: speed and peak memory, fused Triton RoPE vs eager HF apply_rotary_pos_emb, A100 80GB, hidden 16384 (Sec 4.1, Fig 2f/3f)
note: Fused vs eager rope, the same contrast as rope vs rope_fused. Baseline from the repo benchmark script (benchmark_rope.py: transformers apply_rotary_pos_emb); bfloat16 by the script's default; the paper says only 'baseline implementations'. Kernel benchmark, not end-to-end training; Sec 3.3.4 reports a training loss divergence fixed by making tensors contiguous. Added 2026-10-17 because rope is a priority component (T8).

mechanism: removes the positional encoding (NoPE): causal decoders still learn positional information from the attention mask
source: Haviv, Ram, Press, Izsak, Levy (2022), Findings of EMNLP 2022, pp. 1382-1390; Kazemnejad et al. (2023), NeurIPS 2023
published_metric: quality cost: validation perplexity, no positional encoding vs learned (Haviv Table 1)
note: Removal, so not profiled: substituted model energy = baseline minus rope's measured energy (substitute energy 0). Evidence removes all positional encoding, not Pythia's 25% partial rotary. Kazemnejad: similar in-distribution perplexity. Quality is a published estimate, not measured here.
